title: A pianist who played chords by ear, and a saxophonist felled by strokes
summary: Purnell describes a piano player who could not read but played all the chords and sang well, and the speakers recall a saxophone player who had two strokes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: That was the one that learned my brother. Yeah. He put some. I said, see man, when did you start playing piano? Boy was some surprise. That boy says, man, look at this boy. Oh man, I can play. He can't play nothing. Boy come. One time we stopped for a piano player. The piano player got sick of it. He quit or something. He couldn't get nobody. He said, they got here. Boy, that boy, that's such a bad man. See, man.

He said, no, eh? Don't find him. He can't play. Boy, he make all the chords. Everything, bro. He makes everything. Oh, he's a good man, man. I don't know how he's doing now. But he was a chord man, boy. He does very well. All sorts of pieces. Any piece he can play, he'd sing. Oh yeah, oh yeah. Oh yeah. That boy had a devil of voice. He had a what?
He could sing good. He could sing good. Yeah, he sings good. He had a number he used to sing.
A chicken ain't nothing but a boy.

Oh man, he was a boy. See him? He had Boyby Street tied up one time. Man, he used to make all that money, man. Man, that cat boy, he's... Man, that cat, man. He's pretty good. I played with some devil of cats in my days.
I was about another good little saxophone player with it, so I was about to that. Little geesh. Well, yeah, poor boy.
Well, he got a stroke. Yeah, poor boy.
He could play, yeah. He could play. He could play.
He could play. He used to play Kranich too, man.
Yeah, don't forget about that. Leo used to call him the Paul Bones. See, Paul Bones played a better size boy, and Leo used to call him the geesh, I was Paul Bones.

Well, see, when he was playing with Joe Robichelper in Paradise, man, I used to go up there in here, man, and I used to be off, man. I used to go up there, spend my time up there, man. Water cat, water cat could play, boy. Poor boy had two strokes, man. Young boy, too. Very young, yeah. He was young, too.
